title: Execution Gardener: per-arch & seq-len kernel curation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Introduce a lightweight, continuously-updating kernel curation service (codename: Execution Gardener) that maintains per-architecture and sequence-length kernel recommendations. Targets mixed prefill/decode workloads across heterogeneous GPU fleets and supports safe rollouts to Dedicated and Hosted tiers.
background: We currently rely on static kernel-choice heuristics and expensive offline autotuning runs. That leaves tail-latency exposure when model seq-len distributions or hardware mix drift. Execution Gardener aims to reduce per-token cost and 99th percentile latency regressions by maintaining compact fingerprints of workload cohorts and using fast micro-probes + an online bandit to suggest kernel candidates at request time.
approach_summary: Build a small profiling probe that runs cheap microbenchmarks (token-limited warmstart traces) on a tiny subset of requests, aggregate per-tenant and per-route seqlen histograms, maintain a two-level lookup: (1) fingerprint -> ranked candidate list, (2) fallback ladder for quantized/compat kernels. Use a constrained contextual bandit that respects occupancy/SLO masks and can anneal exploration during high load.
design_decisions: Fingerprint granularity: use (arch_family, chiplet_config_hash, median_prefill, median_decode, burstiness_score) instead of per-model hashes to generalize across minor model updates.
Microprobe budget: limit to 0.5% of requests for a given route during ramp; each probe runs two 20-token microbenchmarks (prefill and decode) with lightweight timers.
Bandit objective: multi-armed bandit optimizing 99th-latency and token-cost with a lexicographic priority for SLOs (SLO safety > cost).
Telemetry: store top-3 candidate scores and probe outcomes for offline retraining and manual review; keep retention to 90 days by default.
Safety: deterministic fallback to currently pinned kernel when bandit confidence below threshold and automatic rollback policy tied to latency delta > 10%.
Deployment: start with Dedicated infra alpha, expose flags in Console per-customer; later enable for Hosted with opt-in and white-listing.
Privacy: fingerprints are aggregated and do not include customer prompt tokens or PII; only coarse seqlen stats and occupancy signals are used.
acceptance_criteria: Execution Gardener service deploys to staging and integrates with runtime routing layer.
Microprobe harness performs under 0.5% request overhead on average in canary and collects consistent latency/cost signals.
Bandit candidate chooser reduces average unit-cost by >=3% for the canary routes without violating 99th-latency SLOs (no more than 1% regression during rollout windows).
Console shows per-route kernel recommendations and a simple 'apply' workflow for Dedicated customers.
Automated rollback triggers work end-to-end in simulation and canary runs.
work_items: Proto: implement fingerprint extractor in runtime (C++) and expose via lightweight RPC to gardener service.
Probe: implement microprobe harness and scheduler, add probe sampling logic in router.
Bandit: implement constrained contextual bandit (Thompson variant) with cost + latency reward shaping.
Storage: compact candidate store (Redis LRU) and telemetry sink (timescale for aggregated metrics).
Console: add UI for per-route recommendations, probe status, and manual apply/rollback.
Integration tests: end-to-end canary and rollback tests, stress testing under mixed bursts.
notes: Early simulation shows kernel swaps for short-prefill-heavy routes can cut per-token GPU time by ~6% under balanced occupancy.
A/B experiments should run with seeded traffic to surface edge cases where preferred kernel reduces cost but increases memory pressure on a noisy chiplet.
We prefer a conservative default: Exploration rate annealed to 0.01 under high P95 utilization, 0.05 under low utilization.
Consider a future extension: incorporate quantization fallback profiles and per-tenant cost budget constraints.
Sync with infra team on telemetry retention and Timescale schema before collecting probe buckets.
risks: Probe noise: short microbenchmarks may have high variance on multi-tenant GPUs; mitigate with median-of-3 and occupancy-aware weighting.
Model updates: model architectural changes could invalidate fingerprints; add a model-version tag in telemetry and fall back to conservative choices on version mismatch.
Operational complexity: an online bandit adds new failure modes; provide 'off' switch and require manual approval for Hosted rollouts.
Privacy/regulatory: ensure fingerprints and telemetry are audited to avoid leaking customer data.
implementation_timeline: Week 1-2: runtime fingerprint extractor + probe harness prototype.
Week 3-4: bandit service MVP and candidate store; local and canary tests.
Week 5: Console integration and canary rollout to 3 Dedicated customers.
Week 6-7: extended canary, offline analysis, adjust exploration policy, prepare Hosted opt-in alpha.
Week 8: cross-team review, security audit, and GA plan for Dedicated.
metrics: Per-route unit-cost delta (tokens/GPU-second) - target median -3%+ for canary.
99th-percentile latency change (ms) - must stay within +0% to +5% for safe rollout windows.
Probe overhead (% of requests) - must remain <=0.5%.
Rollout rollback rate - target 0% for production, <=5% during exploratory canaries.
Bandit confidence distribution and candidate churn rate.
